openssl_selection.comment: What the openssl-diagnostic backend asks stock OpenSSL to offer. These are the captured browser ClientHello's exact non-GREASE cipher list, supported-group list, extension set and signature-algorithm list. The emitted-byte gate compares complete JA4, including its protocol/version, SNI, counts and ALPN A component plus the B/C hashes. JA4 sorts extensions and excludes GREASE, and Chrome has permuted its own extension order per connection since v110, so emission order is not a stable target and is not claimed here. What stock OpenSSL still cannot do is place GREASE in the cipher list, supported_groups, supported_versions or key_share; see known_tls_divergence for the exact machine-checked gap.

known_tls_divergence.comment: Machine-checked gap between what the openssl-diagnostic backend offers and the captured browser ClientHello, comparing sets only. All four tracked sets are now closed: OpenSSL 3.5 emits Chrome's exact non-GREASE cipher list, supported-group list, extension set (0x0012/0x44cd/0xfe0d injected via SSL_CTX_add_custom_ext, 0x0005 via SSL_CTX_set_tlsext_status_type, 0x0016 suppressed via SSL_OP_NO_ENCRYPT_THEN_MAC) and signature-algorithm list including the ML-DSA schemes. What remains OUTSIDE these four sets, and is not closable without patching OpenSSL internals: GREASE is absent from the cipher list, supported_groups, supported_versions and key_share (JA4 excludes GREASE, so this does not move JA4); both injected GREASE extensions land at the front rather than first-and-last, because add_custom_ext prepends; extension emission order is fixed rather than permuted per connection as Chrome has done since v110; compress_certificate advertises OpenSSL's zlib+zstd rather than Chrome's brotli; and the two GREASE extension types are fixed per SSL_CTX rather than redrawn per connection, because SSL_CTX_add_custom_ext binds the extension number at registration time. The per-process starting point is drawn from the CSPRNG, so the values vary across installs and restarts, but a single long-lived context reuses them. See tests/test_yume_native_tls_wire.py, which gates complete JA4 equality, re-derives all four declared sets from emitted bytes, and pins this residual gap.
